races.name: Ballylinch Stud Irish EBF Ingabelle Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Timeless Tale
runners_data.note: Won sole start over 6f on Good at two in convincing fashion; McCreery has the horse fresh enough on 20 days and W J Lee takes the ride, suggesting stable confidence — natural prominent racer who should find this stronger pace test navigable if she travels with her customary fluency.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.note: Has won over 6f on Good and shown consistent placing, but this is a step up in trip and Listed class; confirmed front-runner likely to find herself in a three-way pace battle from the off, and her record shows she has been worn down late when the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Broke her maiden over 7f Good last time and has placed over 6f, giving her an encouraging profile for this trip; a genuine prominent-going type who will likely be shuffled back from her natural position by Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque and Lady Patrona forcing the pace — her chance partly hinges on whether she can recover ground from a deeper berth than usual.

runners_data.name: Miss Cashman Hooke
runners_data.note: Finished fourth on debut over 6f on Good for a trainer with a modest 14-day strike rate; natural midfield runner stepping up in class to Listed level with limited evidence — the form-case for her troubling the market is thin at this stage.

runners_data.name: Apollo's Comet
runners_data.note: Dual winner at 7f on Good and was placed at same trip, making the trip and going fit well; a genuine prominent-going horse who, with the race over-subscribed at the head of affairs, will find herself operating further back than she would naturally wish — her best form has come when racing closer to the pace, so treat her displayed map position with caution.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good earlier this season but has been a beaten favourite since, finishing seventh and fourth in subsequent starts; prominent racer whose 29-day break needs to be respected, and whether De Aguiar can find improvement to bridge the gap to the better-credentialled rivals here is uncertain.

runners_data.name: Maire Rua
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and was placed at the same trip, so trip and going are squarely in her favour; Colin Keane takes over in the saddle for Lyons, which is a notable positive — she is a natural prominent runner who will likely be squeezed out of her preferred position by the pace battle ahead of her, meaning Keane must be clever about when to commit.

runners_data.name: Ibelieveicanfly
runners_data.note: OR 100 and Ryan Moore partnership gives this the highest headline rating in the race, but four of five starts have resulted in fourth place on 7f Good — she has a consistent running-on profile from prominent ground, and the strong pace theoretically suits, though her winning form came when the race set up more kindly.

runners_data.name: Snowing
runners_data.note: Two places from four attempts on Good, always prominent but yet to win at the trip; Boudot is a significant booking and the strong pace may draw out a better finishing effort if she can travel smoothly through a truly-run race rather than a falsely run one.

runners_data.name: Blonde Over Blue
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Soft and OR 91, so handles testing ground but the switch to Good is worth noting; confirmed front-runner who will be competing for the lead from gate 8 alongside Bellesque and Lady Patrona — the real question is whether she burns too much energy in that battle to have enough left at the line.

runners_data.name: Bellesque
runners_data.note: OR 91 with a Leopardstown maiden win on her CV over 7f on Good, so course, trip and going all align; another J P O'Brien runner alongside Blonde Over Blue, meaning the yard splits tactics between lead contestants — McDonogh takes the ride and she is proven at this level, but finishing eighth last time on 8f suggests dropping back in trip may sharpen her.

races.paceDynamic: Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque, and Lady Patrona are all confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over Leopardstown's flat 7f, guaranteeing a strong, genuine gallop that will test stamina and compress the early pace into something close to a cavalry charge. With three horses all seeking the same position, the pace will be honest and sustained rather than stop-start, meaning the race is likely to string out and reward horses who can travel comfortably in behind before picking up efficiently in the final two furlongs. The field holds more prominent-type runners than can realistically secure their natural position — Maeda Matsu and Maire Rua are genuine prominent racers but have been mapped back due to congestion at the head of affairs, and they will likely have to settle deeper than they prefer. This shape most directly favours a horse sitting just off a contested lead in the prominent-to-midfield bracket who possesses a clean cruising speed and a reliable finishing kick — a true hold-up profile has less appeal here because the strong pace that should benefit closers is partly illusory given many of the rearward horses are not natural hold-up types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Clean Kick
scenarios.trigger: If Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque, and Lady Patrona fight for supremacy and the gallop is strong throughout, the race sets up for a horse sitting just off the lead with the ability to quicken.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace burns off the front-runners inside the final furlong, and a prominent racer who has travelled smoothly throughout has the energy reserves to assert; Leopardstown's flat 7f punishes those who have over-committed early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lead Thins, One Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Blonde Over Blue or Bellesque — is allowed to dictate a fractionally more controlled tempo while the others fade.
scenarios.body: That runner establishes a clear advantage from halfway and proves too well-organised to reel in, with the field unable to coordinate a clean collective response; OR-rated front-runners with class have done this before at this track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle is fierce enough to exhaust all three protagonists simultaneously and a gap opens up the straight for a closers' run.
scenarios.body: A horse who has been ridden cold and tracks the carnage from midfield picks up strongly in the final furlong when the pace collapses; the flat straight means even late closers can find their way through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steadier Than Expected
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position causes a brief tactical check and the pace is less severe than the three front-runners suggest.
scenarios.body: With a slightly easier rhythm, the race becomes more of a sprint finish from the front, and a horse with raw speed who can latch onto the leaders and sustain it to the line benefits; this is the least likely scenario given the confirmed pace commitments.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque or Lady Patrona establish a clear lead or whether all three lock together — if no one blinks, the pace may become so fierce that none of the three can sustain it to the line.

Maire Rua with Colin Keane is a major jockey booking to flag — if Keane can manoeuvre her into a prominent position despite the congested early stages, she has winning form at exactly the trip and going on offer.

Maeda Matsu is a genuine prominent-going horse mapped back due to pace congestion; if Rory Cleary can find a pocket just behind the pace instead of being stuck wide or deep, her 7f Good form makes her a live threat that her race-map position understates.

Ibelieveicanfly's OR 100 is the highest rated figure in the field but her strike rate of one win from five starts on 7f Good is a concern — Moore will need the pace battle to run perfectly to extract a winning effort from a horse who has finished fourth on four occasions.

Snowing has the Boudot booking and two placed efforts from four Good-ground starts — if the pace collapses in the final furlong she could pick up late, but her overall profile at this level is unproven and she remains one to assess rather than commit to.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Sovereign Path Handicap

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile from draw 11 (neutral), solid placed record on Good going (4/4 similar ground), trained by Sheila Lavery in form (1/8 past 14 days); needs the pace to collapse late in a 21-runner field to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: Carries top weight of 140lbs at OR 101 and steps back to a comfortable 7f; naturally prominent but dropping from 8f assignments where form has been inconsistent on Good — needs to assert early to make weight tell.

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien 3-year-old with a genuine hold-up style and strong Good-ground placed form; last run was a disappointing 5th over 8f at Leopardstown but drops back to 7f which may sharpen him up, drawn wide at 20.

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip on Good going and has been placed at 7f on soft; J P Murtagh stable with Ben Coen aboard — naturally prominent, drawn 16, and the course-and-distance angle is a clear positive here.

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore front-runner with the prestige booking but recent form figures (8-9-4-0-7) are bleak; likely sets a genuine gallop from draw 3 and fulfils a pacemaking role that benefits others more than himself.

runners_data.name: Vafortino
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides this 8-year-old prominent type; placed on Good at 7f last time out, drawn 8, and Charlie Fellowes has 1 from 18 past 14 days — reliable enough to occupy a handy position but placed form may cap ceiling.

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the more in-form of the two likely pace-setters, having won over a mile and been placed over 7f on Good; drawn wide at 18 which means he will need to be ridden forward aggressively early on.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile wearing blinkers, recent form reads 7-7-11-6 — no evidence of ability to compete at this level and a trainer strike rate of 0/2 past 14 days offers little encouragement; hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: Excellent Believe
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this 4-year-old prominent type; hasn't run in 70 days, recent form figures are modest (0-3-3 last three), and drawn 4 with a natural placement close to the pace — fitness question on a long absence.

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 7-year-old prominent type drawn wide at 17; best form has come on Good going over 8f rather than 7f, Kieran Shoemark in the plate, and has shown a placed thread that could keep him involved if he transitions to this trip.

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this genuine hold-up performer with a win at 7f on Good in recent form (1/7f/GOO); drawn 1 on the inside, which may help him slot in economically early, and his profile is authentic for a collapsing-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the widest draw (21) on this hold-up 7-year-old; won over 8f on Good and shows consistent placed form at Leopardstown, but must cover ground from the outside and recent 6th after a 14-day turnaround is acceptable.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: The Scorecard's top selection (low confidence) trained by G M Lyons; his true style is prominent but the volume of pace in this race means he has been redistributed to midfield on the map — five top-three finishes in his last six starts on Good or Soft are the compelling form angle, and if he can travel closer than his mapped position, that consistency becomes very dangerous.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: G M Lyons 3-year-old prominent type with a win at 5f; has been stepping up in distance over 6f recently without convincing, and 7f on Good ground at this OR (89) looks a further stretch — Gary Carroll rides.

runners_data.name: Oro Blanco
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 6f and 7f on Good ground recently, giving him live claims on form, but as a naturally prominent racer with limited space in this congested pace map, he will need to find a lane earlier than the redistributed position suggests to capitalise on those wins.

runners_data.name: Victory Tip
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead 3-year-old returning after 86 days off; won at 8f but runner-up at 8f is most recent positive — the long absence and drop to 7f creates uncertainty, though Declan McDonogh's booking provides some confidence.

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Harrington's 5-year-old has winning form at 9f and placed at 8f on Good — naturally wants to race prominently, but with so many similar types in this field, getting that position in a 21-runner race is the key obstacle rather than lack of ability.

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: The Scorecard danger and arguably the most compelling form profile in the race: three wins in last six including back-to-back 7f wins; Rory Mulligan (5lb claimer) claims further, drawn 15, and trainer John O'Donoghue hits 1/5 in 14 days — naturally prominent with proven 7f Good-ground form.

runners_data.name: Collecting Coin
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this Jennie Candlish 4-year-old who is a true prominent racer; drawn 7, with a win over 8f on Good and placed over 7f on soft, his form profile is solid but the pace-map congestion means he is unlikely to obtain his preferred position without a scrappy early move.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile wearing blinkers for Thomas Gibney, drawn 6; placed at 8f on Good going twice last season and returned 4th after a 14-day break — runs from further back than ideal on this pace shape and must hope the front collapses.

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon takes the ride on this Charlie Johnston 4-year-old who won twice on Standard at 7f but has zero wins in two Good-ground starts; his prominent nature is squeezed by the competitive pace map, and the ground profile is an honest concern for his best form.

races.paceDynamic: Dorset (draw 3, Ryan Moore) and Benevento (draw 18, David Egan) are confirmed front-runners and will press each other from the outset, creating a genuine, honest gallop across seven furlongs of flat Leopardstown turf on Good ground — neither looks likely to yield. This contested early pace should stretch the field and set the race up for horses travelling smoothly in the first half of the race rather than those who need to manufacture their own momentum late. The field holds materially more prominent types than can all secure a position close to the pace: Krasimir, Collecting Coin, Carnival Of Light, Oro Blanco and Dark Viper are true prominent racers but are mapped to midfield given the congestion ahead of them, meaning the genuine prominent slots will be won by Tokenomics, Sindagan, Vafortino, L L Koulsty and the like, while the redistributed horses face a tougher ask. The tactical verdict favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream of a contested pace or those with the cruising speed to sit handy and pounce entering the final two furlongs — efficient, prominent or just-off-the-pace profiles are best served here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset and Benevento set a strong gallop and the race is run at a true clip throughout, horses racing just off the pace in second or third rank benefit most.
scenarios.body: The honest early pace ensures the front two do not steal a soft lead and those tracking at close range can time their runs precisely from the two-furlong pole; L L Koulsty and Sindagan, both natural prominent types with recent winning form over 7f on Good ground, are best positioned to profit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Sustain Lead
scenarios.trigger: If one of Dorset or Benevento is allowed to control the race and the anticipated duel mellows into a soft lead from the front.
scenarios.body: Benevento won over a mile on Good and has clear front-running form at 7f; if the pace dynamic softens mid-race and he is not overly pressured, his stamina edge and recent winning fitness make him a credible finisher from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the honest gallop causes the prominent horses to fade sharply inside the final furlong, creating a collapsing pace scenario that benefits genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Gleneagle Bay (winner over 7f Good) and Fort Vega (multiple placed on similar ground) possess authentic hold-up profiles and are not redistributed types racing out of role, meaning they can deliver a true late run if the front collapses; Rahmi and Andab also carry genuine hold-up form though face the widest draws.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the displaced prominent types — Krasimir, Collecting Coin or Carnival Of Light — manages to secure a better berth than the pace map suggests and travels close enough to challenge.
scenarios.body: Krasimir is the Strand Scorecard selection at low confidence and carries consistent form (five recent top-three finishes), so if the field spreads and he secures a prominent position, his cruising speed is genuine; however, the style-fit discounts make this the least structurally likely shape in a 21-runner field with this much pace congestion.

watchPoints.text: L L Koulsty (draw 15, Rory Mulligan) and Sindagan (draw 16, Ben Coen) sit adjacent in the field and both will attempt to secure prominent positions — watch whether they get clean breaks or interfere with each other in the first two furlongs.

Benevento (draw 18) must cross a wide field quickly to fulfil his front-running role — if he is slow away or gets caught in traffic before the 6f marker, his entire tactical plan unravels and Dorset may be left to front-run solo.

Krasimir's redistribution from prominent to midfield is the key structural risk for Scorecard backers — watch whether G M Lyons has instructed Reese Holohan (7) to push forward regardless or to settle, as the outcome decisively changes his probability of winning.

With 21 runners on a flat 7f track on Good going, the early exchanges will be congested across the width of the course; horses drawn between 13 and 21 (Dark Viper, Benevento, Rahmi, Oro Blanco, Andab) will need to use energy crossing to better ground early — watch whether any of those wide draws visibly cost their runners by the halfway mark.

Excellent Believe returns after 70 days off — watch paddock condition and early race position, as Oisin Murphy will need to find a rhythm quickly from draw 4 if this 4-year-old is to justify the booking on a significant absence.

runners_data.name: Nola Soul
runners_data.note: Top selection on the Strand Scorecard with high confidence; Seamie Heffernan from draw 1 will have no trouble finding a prominent pitch, three-from-three on Good ground including back-to-back wins in July, and the step to 9f suits a filly who already won over 7f in a fast-run heat — everything points the right way.

runners_data.name: Green Dreamer
runners_data.note: Front-runner by style who secured a Listed win over 8f at the Curragh; J M Sheridan partners for Joseph Patrick O'Brien's powerful string, but draw 5 puts him in a scramble against four other pace-inclined rivals and he may find himself consumed by the collective burn-up before the straight.

runners_data.name: Aix La Chapelle
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon takes the mount for Aidan O'Brien on this once-raced winner over 7f on Good; a natural pace-committed type placed into a rearward mapping role simply because the field is saturated with leaders — treat the shown position with caution, as he is not a genuine hold-up performer and his style-fit score of 0.80 reflects that out-of-role assignment.

runners_data.name: Jesus Green
runners_data.note: Colin Keane teams up with Joseph Patrick O'Brien on a colt whose sole run produced a promising second over 8f on Good at the Curragh; the complete absence of a second run means his stamina for 1m1f is an open question, though the 9f pedigree suggests it won't be an issue.

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: David Egan and Charlie Johnston travel from Britain with a colt who finally got his head in front over 8f on Soft at Salisbury last time; four of his five starts have come on Good turf and he handled it competently, but the switch back to Good after that soft-ground win and the step up to 1m1f need proving.

runners_data.name: Victory Speech
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 8f on Good last time under a patient Gavin Ryan for Aidan O'Brien, showing a willingness to go forward from the gate; draw 7 puts him on the outer of the pace scrum and he may not be able to dictate from there with Green Dreamer, Quest For Stars, and Shakespeare all pressing.

runners_data.name: Quest For Stars
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger; James Doyle partners the Appleby three-time winner who has been relentlessly progressive on Good ground — three wins from three, all at 7f-8f, all on Good, all under Doyle — and the key question is whether the 1m1f trip exposes any stamina limit, though Dubawi breeding says it should not.

runners_data.name: Darkness Falls
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore, the most significant jockey booking in the field, takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien on a colt who won over 8f on Good last time after a course third on debut; the 14-day turnaround is the shortest rest in the race but O'Brien regularly fires horses back quickly when they are ready, and Moore's presence upgrades any scenario involving a controlled single lead.

runners_data.name: Shakespeare
runners_data.note: Pierre-Charles Boudot partners Aidan O'Brien's most-experienced runner in this field (three career starts); won over 7f on Good most recently and showed a natural pace-forward tendency — draw 3 gives him every chance to press across and challenge for the early lead alongside Green Dreamer and Victory Speech.

runners_data.name: Zarak Pasha
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh and Joseph Patrick O'Brien team up with a colt whose course-and-distance credentials are the most interesting in the field — won over 9f on Good, which already exceeds today's 1m1f trip, suggesting stamina is a strength rather than a worry; tracked the pace on debut and second run before asserting, a profile that suits a strong-pace race.

races.paceDynamic: Five confirmed front-runners — Green Dreamer, Quest For Stars, Victory Speech, Darkness Falls, and Shakespeare — ensure this 1m1f contest will be run at a relentless gallop from the outset, with no single horse able to dictate comfortably and all five likely to push against each other through the first half-mile. That volume of pace on Good ground over this trip creates a stamina examination in the final two furlongs, where runners who have tracked at a sustainable clip rather than fighting for position will have a decisive energy advantage. Prominent types who can settle just off the boil — specifically Nola Soul and Pikachu — are the primary beneficiaries of this shape, as the lead battle burns through the frontrunners before the home turn. Aix La Chapelle is listed at the rear but is a natural prominent racer pushed back due to the field's pace-heavy profile; of the true leaders, Quest For Stars (unbeaten, Appleby/Doyle) and Darkness Falls (Ryan Moore) are best placed to actually secure the position that matters, though even they face fierce competition for the rail. This race shape strongly favours a prominently-ridden, stamina-confirmed type who avoids the early war and pounces from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners push against each other aggressively from the gate, burning through the field's collective energy reserves before the turn.
scenarios.body: The intense early fractions set up a true stamina test in the final quarter-mile, advantaging those who tracked just off the battle with cover and petrol in reserve. Nola Soul, tracking sweetly from draw 1 with Seamie Heffernan, and Pikachu, whose recent course-form reads 1-3-4, are perfectly positioned to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Quest For Stars or Darkness Falls breaks sharply and secures a lone lead, allowing controlled fractions rather than a contested burn-up.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner settling into their own rhythm on Good ground over 1m1f can produce a potent finishing kick without having wasted energy in early scrimmaging. Quest For Stars — unbeaten in three, all on Good, all ridden with tactical precision by Doyle — is the most dangerous individual if given a soft lead, while Darkness Falls (Ryan Moore, A P O'Brien powerhouse) is an almost equal threat in this mould.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong but not explosive, and a group of prominent racers sweep past the spent leaders together in the straight.
scenarios.body: Zarak Pasha, who won over 9f on Good last time and carries natural stamina credentials, and Jesus Green, second on debut over 1m on Good and deeply unexposed, could both emerge from a prominent berth to challenge late if the race unfolds at a measured but still testing tempo. This scenario requires a middle-paced race that suits rangier types hitting their stride late rather than a true dogfight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Gather
scenarios.trigger: If the pace entirely collapses the front-runners and produces a vacuum that only genuine hold-up horses can fill.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because Aix La Chapelle — the runner mapped to a rearward position — is actually a natural prominent type racing out of role, meaning there are no true hold-up specialists in this field to capitalise. Aix La Chapelle with Soumillon could be the nearest thing to a closer if conditions demand it, but the redistribution caveat must temper expectations sharply.

watchPoints.text: Green Dreamer, Victory Speech, and Shakespeare are all drawn to converge for the early lead from stalls 5, 7, and 3 respectively — watch for significant bumping or checking in the first two furlongs as the pace battle ignites and riders fight for position.

Quest For Stars from draw 8 will need to push across to find a lead role and risks being taken on hard by Darkness Falls and Shakespeare before settling — if Doyle cannot get a clean passage forward early, the unbeaten record may be vulnerable at the first serious test.

Nola Soul breaks from draw 1 which should be favourable, but Seamie Heffernan must avoid being squeezed back by the pace cluster fanning out to her right in the opening furlong — any loss of position from the inside stall in a 10-runner field is a material setback.

Aix La Chapelle has had 51 days off since debut, the longest absence in the race, and Soumillon will be managing a horse racing out of its natural prominent role due to redistribution — the combination of ring-rust and a style mismatch makes Aix La Chapelle one to monitor for signs of flat-footedness out of the gates.

Traffic danger between the 2f and 3f markers is flagged specifically because four prominent-type runners will be trying to hold a position in a 10-horse field moving towards the home turn — watch the rail for any horse being squeezed or forced wide at that critical stage.

runners_data.name: Purview
runners_data.note: D K Weld's four-year-old has won three from three on Good ground and arrives on the back of consecutive wins, form string finishing 1-1; Colin Keane takes the hold-up berth from an outside draw, ideally suited by a strong pace that will be guaranteed here, and this is a horse that consistently improves when the race is truly run.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner for Mrs Harrington who has placed on Good ground but whose recent form shows a string of mid-pack finishes; Shane Foley will push forward from stall 8, but with Arabian Crown on the inside and Thread Of Gold nearby, Green Impact faces a crowded pace battle that may see it spend energy it cannot recover.

runners_data.name: Sons And Lovers
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this consistent O'Brien five-year-old who is proven at 1m4f on Good going and carries top weight of 140lbs; a prominent style suits this race shape if he can slot in behind the pace battle without getting dragged into it, and three placed efforts at this distance on similar ground make him a genuine each-way participant.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' seven-year-old has a lone win on Good ground from seven attempts on similar terrain, but did win on Soft/Standard and has an OR of 108 giving him weight relief; David Egan on a prominent-going type who may not find the pace scenario entirely to his liking, though a patient ride second or third off the pace could see him pick up ground late.

runners_data.name: Arabian Crown
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old is drawn ideally in stall 1 to lead unchallenged onto the rail, though the 1/2 Good-ground record is modest; James Doyle is expert at controlling pace from the front, but with three other front-runners to contend with immediately, Arabian Crown's chance rests heavily on whether the others check each other and allow him a soft lead.

runners_data.name: Piazza San Marco
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on A P O'Brien's three-year-old who has shown front-running tendencies but whose last two runs at 1m4f and 9f both produced placed efforts only; at OR 102 the youngest handicapper in the field, carrying just 127lbs, and Good ground suits, but getting into a pace fight with more seasoned front-runners is a significant concern at this level.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's three-year-old has not run for 76 days, but the yard is firing at 6/56 over 14 days and J M Sheridan keeps the ride; a midfield-style runner who won at 10f on Good and placed at 12f on Good, the stamina profile for 1m4f is the key question, though a truly-run race will at least maximise his finishing kick if the reserves are there.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's four-year-old has won at 12f on Good ground and has tried marathon trips, but the recent form string of 9-1-6 is erratic and the trainer has a 0/35 record in the last 14 days; Gary Carroll rides a hold-up type who needs the pace to create a true test, and the headgear (h) flag suggests connections are trying to sharpen a horse whose recent efforts have been inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: O'Brien's seven-year-old veteran has won and placed over 1m4f on Good ground and arrives on the back of a win last time out, form string ending -1; Declan McDonogh on a midfield type who appreciates a genuine pace and has solid course form, making this consistent staying type a credible place contender if the strong pace scenario plays out.

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's three-year-old ran seventh over 1m4f on Good last time out but had previously won at 10f on Soft; Ben Coen rides a prominent-style horse who has headgear flag (p) and whose jumping form background shows in the trainer's roster — a 87-day absence is the biggest practical concern, and the drop to 1m4f after that run may suit if freshened.

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' lightly-raced three-year-old has won on Good and Soft and shows natural pace, most recently scoring over 12f on Soft; W J Lee takes the mount and will look to press forward, but with Arabian Crown, Green Impact and Piazza San Marco all arriving at similar pace-positions, Thread Of Gold faces a combustible early battle that risks blunting its finishing effort.

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Crown, Green Impact, Thread Of Gold, and Piazza San Marco all carry front-running or pace-pressing tendencies, meaning at least three of them will be fighting for position from the outset over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Leopardstown. With four pace-angles colliding on a flat track, the gallop will be genuine and sustained from flagfall, compressing any tactical advantage for those who try to control tempo — Arabian Crown from stall 1 is best placed to slot onto the rail and lead, with Thread Of Gold and Green Impact likely to press hard in behind or alongside. This strong, honest gallop will test stamina thoroughly, ensuring the race is run out fully from the front and weakening those who have to work early to establish position. The race shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up and late-closing horses with proven stamina who can deliver one sustained run off a true pace — midfield-to-rear profiles with the engine to sustain a finish are at a clear premium here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace among Arabian Crown, Green Impact, Thread Of Gold and Piazza San Marco burns them all off, leaving the race wide open for hold-up types to devour.
scenarios.body: The four pace-setters put each other under pressure from the outset, the fractions are high enough that none can sustain into the straight, and the race becomes a procession for those tracking from midfield or rear; stamina and a clean passage through the field become the decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Front-Runner Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown escapes the early scrummage, settles cleanly in front and controls a comfortable enough tempo that the pace war dissolves before it begins.
scenarios.body: Arabian Crown from stall 1 is ideally drawn to slot onto the rail unchallenged if the others briefly check each other, and a controlled Charlie Appleby-trained horse given a kinder lead can prove surprisingly hard to reel in; James Doyle would dictate terms and conserve enough for a genuine finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suit Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not entirely scorching, allowing a well-positioned prominent racer to sit just off the leader and pounce from a close-up berth.
scenarios.body: Sons And Lovers with Oisin Murphy from a good draw can sit third or fourth without burning petrol, while Gaucher may find the rhythm ideally paced for a horse who excels on Good ground in staying races; both are proven on this surface and trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Favours Pace
scenarios.trigger: If rain freshens the ground or the pace disintegrates through a tactical stop-start pattern that allows a front-runner to steal a winning break unopposed.
scenarios.body: Thread Of Gold's recent winning form on Good ground and natural gate speed give it a sliver of hope if the race fragments rather than flows; this is the least likely shape given four confirmed pace-angle horses making it almost impossible for one to coast.

watchPoints.text: Arabian Crown (stall 1) and Green Impact (stall 8) are on a collision course for the early lead alongside Thread Of Gold and Piazza San Marco — watch the first furlong for physical crowding or early scrimmaging that could unsettle any of the four and compromise their chance before the race finds rhythm.

James J Braddock has been off 76 days and is stepping up in trip to 1m4f for only the second time — watch for signs of inexperience in the straight if the race tests his stamina reserves, as a big run is possible but the fitness question is real.

Purview is attempting 1m4f for the first time despite impressive 10f and 12f wins — watch whether Colin Keane is happy to commit early or deliberately delays until the final quarter-mile, as the trip extension from a hold-up position is the single biggest unknown for the Strand Scorecard selection.

Goodie Two Shoes carries 137lbs as a seven-year-old but has recorded back-to-back top-two finishes over 1m4f on Good ground — watch whether Declan McDonogh can secure a position close enough to the pace to deliver his trademark late run without having to weave through horses in the straight.
In My Teens' trainer Gavin Cromwell has a 0/35 strike rate over the last 14 days — monitor market moves closely, as a drifting price would compound the concern about form and trainer momentum.

runners_data.name: True Love
runners_data.note: AP O'Brien's three-year-old has a sparkling course-and-distance profile (5/5 on similar going, three wins) and Boudot provides a smart European edge; races prominently, likely to slot just behind the pace-setters and is well-drawn in stall 5, making her a key player if the strong gallop suits finishers with pace.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore and AP O'Brien is a formidable combination, and Precise brings a strong record on Good ground (6/6 on similar going, four wins at 8f); hold-up style means she needs the pace to truly collapse leaders, but her last two runs both resulted in victories over this exact trip and going combination.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top selection at high confidence, and the form backs it — four consecutive wins including three at 8f on Good, handled by in-form Colin Keane; prominent style suits this pace scenario perfectly, with the ability to sit just off Fallen Angel and City Of Memphis before asserting a superior turn of foot in the straight.

runners_data.name: City Of Memphis
runners_data.note: Returns from 111 days off but has won three consecutive starts including two at this trip on Good; naturally front-running, she will dispute the lead from the off and if the race develops into a battle with Fallen Angel she may pay for it in the final furlong, though on OR 107 she retains winning claims if she controls fractions.

runners_data.name: Fallen Angel
runners_data.note: Listed as a danger on the Scorecard, and her wins at this track and trip (1/8f/GOO, 1/8f/GOO) keep her firmly in the picture; front-running style with headgear applied, and the question is whether a three-way pace battle dulls her finishing effort — her last two runs were a disappointing 4th and 3rd, suggesting her peak may have passed.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Despite a front-running style, a form string of 402682 and an OR of only 104 in this Group 1 company make it hard to take her at face value as a pace-setter who will hold on; she may briefly share the lead but is most likely to be overtaken by stronger rivals and effectively become a pace-maker for the field.

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Daniel McLoughlin who has won twice at 7-8f on Good ground; 55 days off and an OR of 100 represent steep handicaps in Group 1 company, and she will need a truly exceptional pace meltdown to land a blow from off the bridle.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy brings quality to a three-year-old with a modest recent profile (form -38418); prominent racer whose best win came over 7f on Soft, and the step up to Good ground over a mile in a Group 1 looks demanding — more likely a place candidate than a winner in this field.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old has been prolific at lower levels (four wins in last five) but steps sharply up in class here; hold-up style with Sheridan booked means she needs the pace to be strong enough to mow down Group 1 performers, and the OR of 102 makes that a big ask on debut at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Fallen Angel, City Of Memphis, and Carolina Jetstream all want to lead, guaranteeing a contested, pressured gallop from the outset over Leopardstown's flat mile on Good ground. Fallen Angel (headgear noted) and City Of Memphis are the most likely to actually secure the front rank — Carolina Jetstream's recent form (OR 104, form string 402682) suggests she is unlikely to dominate this grade and may drift back from her ideal position under real pressure. The three-way tussle for the early lead will set a strong tempo, burning through stamina reserves and leaving the race wide open for horses travelling smoothly just off the pace without expending early energy. This race shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield runners who possess a clean turn of foot and can pick off exhausted pace-setters in the final two furlongs — Blue Bolt, travelling prominently under Colin Keane, is ideally cast, while deeper hold-up types stand to benefit if the gallop is truly fierce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Fallen Angel, City Of Memphis and Carolina Jetstream fight each other for supremacy and set a genuinely strong gallop.
scenarios.body: The sustained early pressure bleeds the pace-setters dry in the final furlong, allowing horses who have travelled economically just off or behind the pace to unleash their finishing kicks; Blue Bolt, proven over course and distance at the highest level, is perfectly suited to picking off a strong-run mile on Good turf.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Folds, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-battle between front-runners is severe enough that mid-race carnage opens the race up for a prominent tracker to pounce before the hold-up horses wind up.
scenarios.body: A prominent racer sitting a length or two off the blistering pace absorbs the fractions without overdoing it, then simply outstays the pace-setters as they tie up; Blue Bolt and True Love, both mapped prominent on Good ground they handle well, are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Settles, Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Carolina Jetstream or one of the other front-runners concedes the lead early, reducing the multi-horse battle to a more controlled single pace-setter who dictates comfortable fractions.
scenarios.body: A softer lead by Fallen Angel or City Of Memphis means stamina is not severely tested, allowing a front-runner to conserve enough to hold on from prominent chasers in the straight; Fallen Angel, who has won over course and distance and is experienced at this level, is most likely to seize that benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Launched Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fast that even hold-up horses cannot close the gap despite the leaders weakening, and prominent-to-lead types dominate the finish.
scenarios.body: Duckadilly and Meriden, operating from hold-up positions with bigger gaps to close, find themselves with too much ground to make up despite willing finishes; the race resolves in favour of those who have at least tracked the pace, with Precise benefiting from her Ryan Moore partnership if she improves her position earlier than her H-style suggests.

watchPoints.text: Fallen Angel v City Of Memphis for the lead — if both refuse to concede, expect a genuinely gruelling gallop that could compromise both of their finishing efforts significantly.
Blue Bolt is drawn wide in stall 9 on a flat track; if the early rush for the lead pushes the field across, Keane must avoid getting isolated on the outside and wasting energy covering extra ground.

City Of Memphis returns from 111 days absent — watch her early behaviour in the stalls and whether she travels with her usual fluency, as a rustiness sign could see her swallowed up quickly once the pace is contested.

True Love carries only 128lbs as a three-year-old versus 133lbs for the older horses — the weight allowance could prove meaningful in a stamina-sapping race, and Boudot's positive front-running experience on her (1/8f/GOO, 1/8f/GOO in recent history) adds tactical flexibility.

Meriden's record on identical going (5/11 overall sim-going but 4W in 4 attempts over shorter) suggests the step to 8f in this grade may be the critical unknown — watch whether she travels sweetly into the back straight or begins to struggle for cover.

runners_data.name: Hazdann
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good going 12 days ago for Weld and Chris Hayes; races from hold-up, so needs the front-runners to set a genuine pace, which this field should provide — a repeat of recent form puts him in the finish.|

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien runner with consistent placed form in Ireland; a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the congestion of closers in this field means he is unlikely to get the wide, unobstructed passage he needs, tempering expectations despite the form.|

runners_data.name: Charles Fort
runners_data.note: Low draw (stall 1) is ideal for a natural front-runner stepping back to a mile for Aidan O'Brien and Soumillon; his form is mixed and he was beaten in a Group 1 latest, but his role here is pace-setter and he could steal a race run to his own fractions.|

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Veteran five-year-old for Joseph O'Brien with a modest recent form string — six runs without a win this campaign — and hold-up style means she needs a strong pace to close into; the form figures 725006 do not encourage.|

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the race at 110, six career runs on good ground all resulting in a placing, and Ryan Moore takes the ride — a combination that always commands respect; races from hold-up and is at his best when a true pace presents a gap between the two-furlong pole and the line.|

runners_data.name: Quddwah
runners_data.note: Older horse for Crisford and James Doyle, returning after a 168-day absence; his prominent style and known tendency to fade in the finish are concerns over a flat mile at this level, and the layoff makes him difficult to assess with confidence.|

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: Scorecard top selection on medium confidence; races prominently for the young trainer De Aguiar, won over 7f on good going and has placed form at 8f — his natural style fits this pace scenario perfectly and David Egan is an able partner in a race where prominent racers should hold the advantage.|

runners_data.name: Faiyum
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Lyons and Colin Keane, drawn stall 2, who will press for the lead from the jump; placed form at Group level and consistent recent finishes suggest he is consistent enough to finish in the shake-up even if headed, particularly if Charles Fort tires.|

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for O'Meara with consistent placed form on good ground, including two recent third-place finishes — a prominent racer who should slot comfortably just off Faiyum and Charles Fort and represents solid each-way interest if the pace is as expected.|

runners_data.name: Expanded
runners_data.note: Pierre-Charles Boudot takes the ride on this Aidan O'Brien-trained four-year-old returning from a 118-day break; placed in two of his last three and a prominent racer by nature — the layoff is the key unknown, but he is capable of a bold show fresh.|

races.paceDynamic: Faiyum and Charles Fort are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both drawn low (stalls 2 and 1 respectively), they will contest the lead from the outset on Leopardstown's flat mile, creating a genuine and honest gallop rather than a tactical crawl. Four of the ten runners — Faiyum, Charles Fort, Quddwah, Power Blue, Audience, and Expanded — all want to race prominently, meaning there will be significant early jostling for position through the first two furlongs, with congestion a real danger two to three out as that group compresses. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; Faiyum and Charles Fort are most likely to actually secure the front positions given their natural lead style and low draws, while Audience, Quddwah, and Power Blue will need to settle for second rank. A genuine, contested pace on good ground over a flat mile at Leopardstown classically suits prominent-to-midfield gallopers who can travel smoothly just off the pace and produce a sustained run through the final two furlongs — late closers from the rear will have ground to find, but the honest tempo should ensure the strong hold-up horses are not left behind either.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum and Charles Fort set an honest pace and the prominent stalkers travel smoothly just behind them.
scenarios.body: Power Blue and Audience track the contested lead at a comfort­able two lengths, hit the rising tempo approaching the final two furlongs and sustain their effort to the line; good ground and a flat track reward horses that avoid early trouble and produce a clean, progressive finish. This shape suits Power Blue, whose course-form and prominent style align perfectly, and Audience, who has consistent form placing close up on similar going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out and a true strong pace unfolds, allowing hold-up horses to close powerfully.
scenarios.body: Isaac Newton, the highest-rated closer in the field and six-from-six on good ground, is delivered wide and late by Ryan Moore and cuts through tiring rivals; Hazdann, fresh off a recent win on this exact going, also finds clear daylight to finish strongly. This shape is the one where the Scorecard's top danger Isaac Newton makes most appeal, and Hazdann — who has solid good-going form — can follow him home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort or Faiyum steals a march at a controlled tempo and is never seriously challenged for the lead.
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners, most likely the low-drawn Charles Fort under Soumillon, dictates an unhurried gallop and quickens decisively from two furlongs out before hold-up horses can organise their challenge; Faiyum, racing prominently as the other pace-setter, is best placed to chase the winner if the gallop is only moderate. A slow-burn scenario suits horses on the pace, and neither closer nor prominent stalker gets into the race in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding disrupts prominent types and a gap opens centrally in the straight for a midfield move.
scenarios.body: Congestion between two and three furlongs out shuffles back several prominent horses, gifting the midfield runners a clean passage when it matters; Expanded, given a patient hold by Boudot after a long break, could benefit from a clear run, while Cowardofthecounty — a genuine hold-up type forced into midfield by the race shape rather than any tactical choice — may find late momentum if the tempo is true. This is a lower-probability shape because it depends on disruption that may not materialise and on horses racing in constrained positions.

watchPoints.text: Faiyum and Charles Fort will lock horns from stall 2 and stall 1 — watch whether one concedes the lead early or whether they race head-to-head for the first three furlongs, as the latter outcome burns stamina and leaves the door open for closers.

Prominent congestion between stalls 3–5 (Quddwah, Power Blue, Audience) creates a real risk of interference or a check two to three furlongs out — any horse caught in traffic at that stage is likely to lose their chance on a flat mile with limited time to recover.

Isaac Newton is drawn widest of all in stall 10 — Ryan Moore will need to decide early whether to drift back and come widest of all late, or push up to save ground; a flat mile with good ground gives him the conditions he wants, and his finishing kick is the biggest single threat to the prominent horses.

Quddwah is returning from 168 days off and has a recorded tendency to fade in the finish — if he takes a prominent position and weakens, he could hamper rivals arriving with late runs between the one-furlong and two-furlong markers.

The going is a consistent Good across all races today at Leopardstown with no variance between distances — no ground bias is indicated and the surface should ride fairly for all styles, meaning pace rather than ground exploitation will be the decisive factor.

runners_data.name: Constitution River
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's mount for Aidan O'Brien carries strong credentials — two wins from three Good-ground starts at 10f — and from draw 3 Moore can settle just behind the pace melee, making him a prime beneficiary if the front-runners exhaust each other.

runners_data.name: Wimbledon Hawkeye
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent racer by record whose mapping to the rear of the field reflects redistribution due to a pace-heavy field, not his instinct; Soumillon will likely find himself shuffled back if the three confirmed leaders take over early, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in his finishing effort from an unnatural position.

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top pick and the classiest of the three confirmed pace-setters; Colin Keane partners a three-year-old with four wins on Good ground, and if she can assert herself over Hotazhell and Hawk Mountain to control the fractions, her proven ability to dictate and quicken makes her genuinely dangerous.

runners_data.name: Hotazhell
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing headgear (p — probably hood/pads), absent 48 days, and without a win in three Good-ground outings; likely to push hard for early supremacy but her recent form (form string 40-D31) and absence raise questions about whether she can sustain that effort.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Prominent-going O'Brien runner who has been off 49 days and whose best trips appear to be 12f-plus; likely to be closer to mid-pack than usual given the pace dynamic, and the step down in trip from his recent 12f+ runs is a stamina consideration in reverse — he may lack the zip of shorter-distance rivals.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Susie
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's Strand danger flag is well-supported: five runs on Good ground with 1W4P and a progressive profile at 10f; Oisin Murphy will look to hold a prominent position just behind the chaos of the pace war, and the consistent placed form in similar conditions marks this three-year-old as a genuine live danger.

runners_data.name: Hawk Mountain
runners_data.note: The third confirmed front-runner for Aidan O'Brien, drawn 5, but only two of four similar-going runs have placed and none have won at this trip; likely to be swallowed up in the pace battle with Item unless he can slot in behind early, making him more of a pace contributor than a winner.

races.paceDynamic: Item, Hotazhell, and Hawk Mountain all want to lead, guaranteeing a genuine, pressured gallop from the outset over Leopardstown's flat 1m2f on Good ground — there will be no gift of a slow early pace here. Item (Colin Keane, Andrew Balding) is the highest-rated of the front-runners and has the class and recent form to boss the pace battle, while Hotazhell and Hawk Mountain will push her throughout the early and middle stages, ensuring every runner is asked a stamina question entering the straight. With three genuine leaders fighting for position and a true pace assured, this race shape strongly favours hold-up and mid-division runners who can conserve energy before unleashing a sustained late run — closers and prominent racers with a strong galloping action through Good ground are the primary beneficiaries. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than can all realistically secure a forward position; of the prominent horses, Constitution River (Ryan Moore) and A Boy Named Susie (Oisin Murphy) have the class and jockey calibre to hold prominent ground, while Lambourn and Wimbledon Hawkeye are more likely to be shuffled back than their natural style would suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Item, Hotazhell, and Hawk Mountain battle for lead, burning each other out through a genuine pace war.
scenarios.body: The fierce early tempo sets up a strong late-run, with the field strung out and the principals fading inside the final furlong; horses who have settled mid-division or just off the pace and possess the stamina to pick up late are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Item Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Item asserts dominance early and the other pace rivals submit, allowing her to dictate at a controlled but honest gallop.
scenarios.body: Item uses her class advantage over Hotazhell and Hawk Mountain to dictate a sustainable tempo, then quickens decisively in the straight before rivals can mount a challenge; her 4W4P record on similar Good ground and Strand top-pick status underline this threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war moderates mid-race and prominent types like Constitution River and A Boy Named Susie track the leaders efficiently.
scenarios.body: Constitution River and A Boy Named Susie use their tactical speed to sit just behind the leading trio, saving ground and pulling clear of the hold-up horses; Ryan Moore's positional intelligence on Constitution River and Oisin Murphy's aggressive front-foot riding on A Boy Named Susie make this combination particularly dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so ferocious that even prominent horses are compromised, leaving only the deepest closers with energy reserves.
scenarios.body: Almaqam, ridden patiently from draw 8 and with proven form at this trip on Good ground, powers home late; however, this scenario is structurally discounted because Wimbledon Hawkeye — nominally mapped to the rear — is not a natural hold-up type and is unlikely to deliver a true closer's challenge.

watchPoints.text: Item, Hotazhell, and Hawk Mountain all breaking from draws 4, 1, and 5 — watch the first 2f for a potential three-way pace battle that could fundamentally alter the entire race shape.

A Boy Named Susie (Oisin Murphy, draw 2) is the Strand's flagged danger and must be tracked from early; if Murphy secures a prominent position just behind the pace leaders without getting embroiled in the war, this horse is dangerous entering the straight.

Wimbledon Hawkeye is mapped to hold-up but is naturally a prominent racer — watch whether Soumillon is forced back further than planned by the early pace rush, as racing out of role from draw 7 significantly complicates his chance.

Hotazhell is 48 days off the track and equipped with headgear; if she fires early and then capitulates rapidly, she could cause interference or stop suddenly in front of hold-up horses tracking her run.

Lambourn's 49-day absence and preference for 12f-plus trips at a genuine 1m2f pace — watch whether Declan McDonogh elects to drop him in mid-field from the outset rather than fight for his natural prominent berth.

runners_data.name: Helvic Dream
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old midfield type with good-ground form at Leopardstown and over long trips, but recent form figures of 3700-9 show a horse well past his best and hard to trust in a 26-runner competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Sunny South West
runners_data.note: A consistent placer at 12f-20f, this horse is a natural front-runner in reality but the pace surplus pushes it back through the field; its best efforts have come when travelling prominently, so a genuine midfield role here is not ideal.

runners_data.name: The Reverend
runners_data.note: Long absence of 223 days is the dominant concern; trained by Mullins and capable of arriving fresh, but jumping from a headless heat to a 26-runner Leopardstown handicap after over seven months off demands respect for fitness question marks.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners who will force the pace from the off; a three-year-old trained by Charlie Johnston stepping up significantly in trip and field size, and the question is whether the gallop he creates suits him or burns him out by the straight.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old with back-to-back wins and a prominent style that has served well at shorter trips; Shane Foley retains the ride and if the field splits enough for Wyman to take a natural prominent position, the step to 1m5f is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 1m4f on soft and 1m1f, this prominent-style six-year-old carries a big weight of 133lbs and comes back after 43 days; the strong pace suits horses with staying ability but the burden at the top of the handicap is a real risk.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist from the Joseph O'Brien yard who won over 1m5f on good at Leopardstown and returns to that course and distance; lightly raced at this trip and likely to arrive late with a clear run as the leaders fold in a strong-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Cannes
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence; a three-year-old carrying 127lbs for Colin Keane and Joseph O'Brien with good-ground form at 1m4f, who should get a prominent position off the well-heated pace and has the profile to outstay rivals in the straight.

runners_data.name: Poetic Sound
runners_data.note: A horse with one win over 1m4f on good but whose most recent form figures show 17th and 7th on softer ground; the step to 1m5f on a testing gallop may suit the stamina side, though the 137lb burden is the most significant obstacle.

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon
runners_data.note: A horse that won over 1m4f on good at Leopardstown and races prominently; the slow recent form (071004) including several double-figure finishes in the last year raises questions about whether that form can be replicated at this level in a 26-runner field.

runners_data.name: Yousaynothingatall
runners_data.note: A lightly weighted three-year-old with six runs and two wins for Oisin Murphy and O'Brien; form includes wins over 1m-1m2f and a prominent style that should slot in just off the pace — stamina over 1m5f remains the only query on a horse that is very much on the upgrade.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: Identified as a key danger on the Strand Scorecard and rightly so; two wins on good ground over 1m and 1m2f with a W J Lee partnership, and recent form of 941-12 shows a horse in excellent shape — the stamina extension to 1m5f is the one thing to prove.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: Three wins from recent starts including over 1m4f on good ground, this three-year-old goes without a declared jockey which is immediately notable; will force the pace alongside Evanesco and Madbadanddangerous, and whether there is enough left in reserve after that early commitment is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this Mullins-trained hold-up horse but six consecutive finishes of 3-6th on good ground at similar trips tell a consistent story of nearly-but-not-quite; hard to see the dynamic changing markedly in a 26-runner field at this OR.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Won over 1m3f on good ground and races out of the hold-up box; Seamie Heffernan is an important booking but recent efforts include 13th and 15th at shorter trips, and the trainer has a quiet 14-day strike rate — needs everything to go right late.

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien on this prominent-style three-year-old who finished second over 1m on good at Leopardstown; stepping up significantly to 1m5f and facing a surplus of pace pressure, the trip extension is the crux and Moore's patient handling may serve him well if the stamina is there.

runners_data.name: This Songisforyou
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse with James Doyle in the saddle and a second place over 1m2f on good in recent history; the 43-day layoff and recent 550-29 figures suggest a horse that needs to find a bit extra at this level, though the pace scenario does create the late-run opportunity he needs.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 1m2f on soft, this horse's natural inclination is to race forward but with so many prominent types competing for space, it will realistically be shuffled back; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in its showing from an unfamiliar position.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old noted as a Strand Scorecard danger and with recent back-to-back seconds in good-ground form; by nature a prominent racer, the crowded pace scenario means the seven-pound claimer Reese Holohan will likely find it racing further back than ideal, which slightly softens its prospects despite the strong recent profile.

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Second of the confirmed pace-setters from the Noel Meade yard; a three-year-old who has won over 1m2f-1m3f and will push the tempo hard from draw 20 — if the pace burns the others out without destroying him, he can compete deep into the straight, but that self-destructive dynamic is the biggest risk.

runners_data.name: Night Moon
runners_data.note: A proven winner over 1m4f on good ground and a natural front-runner-to-prominent type; the field's pace surplus pushes it back through the field from draw 1, and Andrew Slattery must navigate a very different tactical race from what this horse ideally wants.

runners_data.name: Factual Fact
runners_data.note: Twice a winner over 1m4f-1m5f on good ground for De Bromhead with a 22-day turnaround; though it naturally wants to be prominent, the seven-pound claimer Conor Cusack rides and the overcrowded pace map means a wider, deeper run than ideal — the form with three placed efforts in five recent starts is solid and the trip suits.

runners_data.name: Dawn Rising
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old midfield specialist whose form figures of -80780 tell the story bluntly; even a strong pace that theoretically suits closers has not coaxed improvement from this horse, and at OR 96 in a 26-runner handicap, the profile is hard to endorse.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: A four-year-old who has won twice over 1m on good ground but is naturally suited to a prominent position; pushed back in this pace-heavy field under a five-pound claimer, the STYLE_FIT concern is real and the step to 1m5f on this occasion is an additional query.

runners_data.name: En Or
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up type returning just five days after last run, which is remarkably quick; best effort in recent history was a second over 1m4f on good, but trainer Martin has a quiet recent strike rate and the very short turnaround makes it hard to build a confident case.

runners_data.name: Glenroyal
runners_data.note: A four-year-old from O'Brien's yard who won over 1m3f and 1m on good ground but has finished 8th, 19th, and 7th in three subsequent efforts; Chris Hayes rides and the headgear flag (p) suggests an attempt to recover form — capable on best showing but form has dropped off sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco, Madbadanddangerous, and Minella Rockett will push hard for the lead from the off, guaranteeing a strong, sustained gallop over this 1m5f flat Leopardstown trip on good ground — there will be no dawdling, no tactical crawl. That relentless early pace will stretch the field significantly inside the first half-mile, testing stamina hard and likely burning off any horse who over-commits in tracking the speed. Horses with genuine staying power who can settle midfield or just off the pace — conserving energy while the pace-setters do the damage — are the primary beneficiaries of this shape; free-running types who chase the speed without purpose will be cooked. The field also contains a surplus of prominent racers: among those most likely to actually secure a forward position are Cannes, Wyman, Port Of Spain, and Counting Coup, while Factual Fact, Star Harbour, Night Moon, Diamond Exchange, and Sunny South West are true prominent types who will be pushed further back than usual and cannot rely on getting their natural berth in such a contentious pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Blows Apart Field
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco, Madbadanddangerous, and Minella Rockett send it from the off and the gallop becomes truly searching from the first furlong.
scenarios.body: The three leaders press each other relentlessly, turning the race into a genuine slog of stamina; horses who have settled midfield with a clean clear run emerge with full tanks late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracked Leaders Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders gains a slight advantage early and the pace, while strong, remains honest rather than suicidal.
scenarios.body: A prominent tracker travelling well within themselves into the straight benefits as the leader ties up; a horse with a forward position and a sharp turn of foot over this trip kicks and holds on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Storms Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly brutal and the leaders completely empty out inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A patient midfield or hold-up horse with proven stamina swoops under a strong jockey ride; the closing sectionals become very fast as the front rank capitulates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the declared front-runners is withdrawn or fails to stride on, leaving a false pace and a bunched, tactical contest.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish from an unusually slow early pace, favouring a horse with tactical speed who can quicken off a slower tempo rather than grind relentlessly.

watchPoints.text: Evanesco, Madbadanddangerous, and Minella Rockett — watch whether all three genuinely press from the off or whether one drops away early, as the degree of early pace directly determines how far back the field is strung out and how much energy is left for the principals late.

Cannes under Colin Keane — watch for whether Keane can slot into a prominent but covered position off the hot pace without being shuffled wide or checked in a 26-runner field, as the Strand Scorecard selection's chance depends heavily on getting that clean prominent run.

Star Harbour with Reese Holohan (7lb claimer) — a horse that wants to race forward in a field with multiple confirmed pace-setters; watch how the inexperienced rider handles the first two furlongs when pace is fierce and positions are fiercely contested.

races.paceDynamic: Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby are the two confirmed pace-setters, and with eight of nineteen runners wanting a prominent position, the early stages over Leopardstown's flat mile will be crowded and competitive rather than leisurely — an honest gallop is the likeliest outcome. That sustained pace through the middle portions of the race sets up a test of genuine stamina and class rather than sprint speed, favouring runners who can travel smoothly in the first third and quicken through the final two furlongs without having burned their reserves. The congestion between two and three furlongs out is the key danger zone for prominent runners who find themselves pocketed in double-figure fields. This race shape most favours a well-positioned, mid-to-prominent type with a clean passage — not a hold-up horse needing a deep closing run on ground that does not accelerate sharply. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure that position; Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby are most likely to actually lead, while Bella Colombia and Anvika — though natural front-end or prominent racers by instinct — are mapped to midfield because the pace queue leaves them no room, tempering their chances in a shape that rewards position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby set an honest gallop that stretches the field and the prominent group tracks them into the straight.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn out their rivals through a genuine pace, and a horse sitting just off the speed in the first four survives the traffic scrimmage two out to score; Rebel Wave's recent back-to-back wins over 7f at this level on good ground and draw one to race prominently suit this shape exactly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the contest pace is faster than it looks and the front two fade turning in, releasing midfield runners who have travelled kindly.
scenarios.body: Mallavelly, Tachos or Drop Dead Gorgeous — horses who naturally settle behind the scrimmage — pick up the pieces as the leaders capitulate inside the final two furlongs; Ryan Moore on Drop Dead Gorgeous has the tactical intelligence to exploit a pace collapse with a perfectly timed run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leaders Outstay, Front-End Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves sustainable rather than burning — a true honest gallop at even tempo — and one of the front pair or a rider who slots in second-row early simply gallops rivals into the turf.
scenarios.body: Thrifty Of Digby has recent winning form over this distance on good ground and has demonstrated front-running authority; Guardian Of Realm won over 10f before stepping back in trip and may simply stay the pace better than rivals expect.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Gets Run
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues scramble the prominent group two out and a clean-passaged hold-up horse threads through late.
scenarios.body: Tahcawin and Pink Oxalis are genuine hold-up types but need a stop-start gallop to create the gap; the deep field and flat Leopardstown track make a sustained gallop more likely than the pace-break their profiles require, so this remains a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Bella Colombia and Rebel Wave both want prominent positions from opposite sides of the draw (7 and 1) — watch whether Bella Colombia gets shuffled back at the break, as failure to secure her natural berth materially downgrades her winning chance.

Guardian Of Realm (draw 13) and Thrifty Of Digby (draw 14) are the two front-runners setting the pace; if one of them is taken on by the cluster of eight prominent horses and the gallop becomes a burn-up, watch for both leaders to capitulate sharply inside the final furlong.

The traffic flashpoint two to three furlongs from home in a 19-runner flat mile on Leopardstown's turning straight could cost several prominent runners their rhythm — watch Suzie Songs and Aviatrice specifically, as both need a clean passage to show their best.

Electric Beauty has been off 93 days and faces a trip shorter than her recent winning and placed distances (9-10f); watch the market to see whether stable confidence or public uncertainty dominates before post time.

Drop Dead Gorgeous (Ryan Moore, 14 days since last run) may be the one horse in the hold-up group with a jockey capable of threading through traffic in the straight — watch where Moore positions her in the first half-mile, as any prominent move would shift the calculus entirely.
